rules.rule:
This is ESP32 firmware for a squash scoreboard. ONE source tree builds TWO boards, selected by -DBOARD_REV: V1 = ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N16R8 on V2's pinout (envs v1 / v1_ota, BOARD_REV=1, 112 WS2812B LEDs, OLED, no e-paper, battery sense) and V2 = ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N16R8 (env v2, BOARD_REV=2, 74 LED slots, e-paper, battery). The reviewer's goal is real bugs, on EITHER board. The overriding priority is: will the V1 unit still work, and can it still be recovered, after flashing this code? V2 correctness bugs matter too. Not code beauty.

THE UNRECOVERABLE FAILURE: V1 is sealed. Its ONLY practical flash path is OTA over WiFi (env v1_ota). USB flashing needs physical disassembly; the first flash of a naked board is the one-time v1_bootstrap image. So any change that leaves V1 booting WITHOUT a working WiFi + OTA server is a BRICK. Report those as critical.

Flag, as CRITICAL:
- Any change to the layout, size, field order or packing of PrefsData (src/PreferencesManager.h). read() rejects the stored NVS blob unless getBytesLength == sizeof(PrefsData). A rejected blob silently reverts to defaults, and enableDevMode defaults to 0, which means no STA, no AP, no OTA, no telnet on next boot. That is the brick.
- Any new field added to PrefsData for the same reason, including one added 'harmlessly' at the end.
- Any change to board_build.partitions, the partition CSV, flash size, or anything moving the NVS partition offset. OTA writes only the app image; the device keeps its own old partition table, so a mismatch loses the WiFi credentials.
- Any code path where enableDevMode == 0 prevents WiFi/OTA from ever coming up on V1 with no remote-only recovery route.
- The OTA board marker (src/BoardMarker.*, helpers/check_firmware_image.py): V1 rejects images without a V1 marker, so anything that stops a correctly marked V1 image from being accepted (marker not linked at image offset 0x120, board_marker dropped by the linker - keep `-Wl,-u,board_marker`, marker value/magic changed on one side only, the check made stricter than the tool verifies) makes every future OTA fail and is a BRICK. A V2 image must never be accepted by V1. V2 accepting unmarked legacy images is intentional.
- Anything that can make the firmware boot but be unable to RECEIVE a further OTA update (a hang, a watchdog reset loop, a crash before the web server starts, a blocking call in setup() before OTA is serving).
- Anything that makes setup() or loop() able to crash, assert, abort or infinite-loop on V1 specifically.

Flag, as HIGH:
- Growth in the app image toward the 6.25 MB app0/app1 slot limit (default_16MB.csv), and any heap/stack growth that could exhaust internal RAM (new large static buffers, std::vector reserves, 32-profile rosters, big PROGMEM tables, web UI string building). Both boards have 8 MB PSRAM but the Arduino core does not use it for the heap by default.
- V2-only hardware code reachable on V1: e-paper, battery ADC, GPIOs used differently on V1, hardware V1 does not populate (e-paper); both boards are S3 so IDF availability is the same.
- Missing or wrong '#if BOARD_REV' guards. BOARD_REV conditionals are allowed ONLY in src/Board.h and hardware wrapper headers (DisplayProfile.h, LedDisplay.h, LedCentralScreenBorder.h, Animation/LedSweepAnimation.h, Animation/LedSlotPositions.h, EInk/EInkDisplay.h, EInk/Images/PlayerSetupQr.h, BatterySensor.h). Never in views, modes, Tournament, Match, Game, Rules. Wrappers must keep identical APIs on both boards, with empty stubs on V1.
- A V1 stub that is not actually inert: an empty setter whose ARGUMENT still gets evaluated and does real work or touches absent hardware, a stub returning a value a caller then dereferences, or a stub that compiles but returns a wrong default.
- Array indexing, LED indices or slot numbers derived from V2 geometry (74 slots, 9-segment modules, dead slots 12/28/44/60) being applied on V1 (112 LEDs, 7-segment, history bar at index 88). Out-of-bounds writes into the FastLED buffer.
- Anything that could regress the V1 LED output: FastLED must stay pinned at 3.9.16 and the platform at espressif32@6.13.0 (Arduino core 2.0.17). Newer cores switch FastLED to its RMT5 driver and corrupt the WS2812 stream (re-test on S3 is a separate task).
- Long or blocking work in loop() on V1, which starves the OTA/telnet handling and the RMT refill.

Flag, as MEDIUM:
- 'static constexpr' array data members in header-only classes: these are an ODR link error on GCC 8.4 / C++14, which is this toolchain. They must be local constexpr variables inside the static method.
- Uninitialised members, off-by-one in glyph/segment loops, loops bounded by a hardcoded widest-segment count instead of SegmentTable.count.
- Anything V1-visible that changes behaviour the user did not ask for.

Do NOT report: pure style, naming, comment density, missing unit tests, 'use smart pointers / STL algorithms / RAII' advice, const-correctness, or speculative issues without a concrete failure. Static allocation and raw pointers are deliberate here. Favour precision: stay silent unless you can name the concrete V1 failure.

Also flag (HIGH), both boards: the roster editor (src/Web/PlayerSetupWebUi.h, PlayerSetupMode, RemoteDevelopmentService) is shared by both boards. GET /update is the only route that serves the WiFi-credentials form, and POST /update is the OTA upload; either becoming unreachable, gated or double-registered on V1 is CRITICAL. Leaving PROFILE must return the device to STA + OTA without a reboot when enableDevMode is on. Per-segment brightness compensation (V2) must scale pixels in place exactly once per frame before FastLED.show(), must never compound, and must leave V1 output byte-identical.

Phone-only web pages served gzipped from the firmware (PROFILE roster editor, settings, firmware/WiFi update page). Flag: anything that breaks /update (firmware upload or WiFi credentials form) outside PROFILE - that is how sealed V1 is recovered (CRITICAL); posts that are not application/x-www-form-urlencoded; more than one preview request in flight; a preview left applied on the device after cancel/navigation; UI text that must be Polish with real diacritics; fetch error paths (503 when PROFILE is shut must show the note and keep nav usable). These sources are kept readable and minified at build time by helpers/web_assets.py (jsmin rules): flag JS template literals (the build rejects them) and any construct whose meaning depends on whitespace or line breaks. When a diff is a reformat, flag only behaviour that differs from the previous version. Do not report style.

Pre-build and generator scripts. A pre: extra_script runs on every firmware build. Flag: a script that can emit a partial or stale generated header without failing the build; nondeterministic output (timestamps, dict order) that forces rebuilds; writing files on every build when content is unchanged; version bumps from test envs; Windows path / encoding bugs (UTF-8 BOM, CRLF); a raw NUL written into a source file. web_assets.py also minifies JS/CSS/HTML before gzip, and a minifier bug ships silently broken pages: flag any input where minified output differs in meaning from the source - JS newlines that ASI depends on, regex literal vs division detection (incl. after keywords such as return/typeof), '+ +' / '- -' spacing, comment markers inside strings or regexes, CSS whitespace that is significant (descendant combinators, values, calc), HTML whitespace between inline content; and any unsupported construct that is accepted instead of failing the build. Do not report style.

PlatformIO Unity host tests (native_v1/native_v2), header-only includes from src/, C++11. Flag: a test that cannot fail (asserting a value against itself, loops that never run, a golden compare that passes on missing/empty files or on a line-count mismatch); coverage silently narrowed vs what the name claims; fixtures opened in text mode (CRLF); tests depending on cwd; platformio.ini test_ignore mistakes that would let `pio test` target a firmware env (would flash Unity images, incl. OTA to sealed V1 = CRITICAL). Do not report style.
